within stronger storms, but lightning outside of rain cores
continues to be a concern.

quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.

* THUNDERSTORMS...Scattered coverage with abundant lightning.

* OUTFLOW WINDS...Gusty, erratic winds up to 40 mph.

events.summary:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...For Highway 30 counties and areas south to the Missouri
border in central Iowa.

* WHEN...Through Saturday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur
in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Several rounds of rain have brought 2 to 6 inches of rain to
central Iowa this week. Additional rainfall is forecast later
tonight into Saturday morning. The combination of
saturated soils and high rainfall rates may overwhelm
capacity, which will increase flooding potential.

events.summary:
FFWBOU

The National Weather Service in Denver has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
North Central Elbert County in east central Colorado...

* Until 900 PM MDT.

* At 739 PM MDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain 13 miles south of Byers, or 34
miles northwest of Limon, moving northeast at 5 mph. Between 1 and
5 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5
inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing
or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, gulches,
roads, and poor drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of North Central Elbert County.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Comanche Creek, Spring Branch, Wilson Creek, East Bijou Creek, Hay
Gulch, West Bijou Creek and Middle Bijou Creek.
